articles.title: Nintendo Rules Out Further Switch 2 Price Rises as Console Sales and Profit Fall
articles.summary: Nintendo has ruled out further Switch 2 price rises while reporting falling console sales and reduced profit. According to Bloomberg, operating profit fell 16% to 73.9 billion ‌yen (approx. $467 million) during the three months to September 30, off the back of a 15% decline in sales.
body: Despite this, Reuters reported that Nintendo President Shuntaro Furukawa insisted Nintendo had enough memory to meet its forecasted Switch 2 sales of 16.5 million units for the financial year ending March 2027, and is not considering further price changes.

Nintendo launches the Ocarina of Time remake today, and investors are hoping it will boost sales of the Switch 2 during the holiday sales season. Reuters said that investors remain concerned that the memory situation, as well as a “lack of high-profile titles” for Switch 2 this year, could negatively affect the console's momentum.

Nintendo's financial report reveals data for the first half of the current financial year, (from April to September 2026). During that six month period, Nintendo sold 6.49 million Switch 2 units, down from the 10.36 million it sold during the same period last year.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Changes to the Infamous Water Temple Are Actually Brilliant
articles.summary: With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ’s Switch 2 remake out now, long-time Nintendo fans are in for a lot of warm nostalgia. A trek through the lost woods, duets with Sheik, a return to the Bombchu Bowling Alley — all of those wonderful moments return in a faithful remake that feels every bit…
body: Don’t worry! Even though the Ocarina of Time remake is careful not to change too much about the original game, it does make some small tweaks to a dungeon that still haunts a generation. It’s mercifully easier to navigate now thanks to a few minor but smart updates that go a long way.

While that structure hasn’t changed much in the remake, Nintendo does make it easier to get through with a few smart decisions. That came at the request of Eiji Aonuma, who directed the original Ocarina of Time. “I had some overdue homework: I wanted to do something about the Water Temple I created 28 years ago,” Aonuma said in a recent Nintendo developer interview. “Since it became well known for its difficulty in the original game, I had the team make some adjustments in this version.”

One of those adjustments just comes down to clearer signposting. Building off the dungeon’s Ocarina of Time 3D redesign, the doors that lead to water controls are now clearly marked with symbols showing you exactly how the water level will change. You no longer have to remember which door leads to the room that drains the room, or which one will get you to floor two.

articles.title: Adam Driver Confirms His Role in Heat 2, Comments on Recent Michael Mann Shooting
articles.summary: Adam Driver has confirmed his role in Heat 2, and commented on director Michael Mann's recent shooting accident. Appearing on an episode of The Rich Eisen Show, Driver confirmed to the host that he will be playing the role of Otis Wardell in Mann's upcoming follow-up to the 1995 crime film.
body: Driver also expressed enthusiasm at being reunited with Mann, who he previously teamed up with on the 2023 motor racing biopic, Ferrari.
"Heat is a masterpiece," Driver told Eisen. "I love Michael, I loved working with him [on] Ferrari, but working on this? I'm excited. The cast is so awesome."

Driver also mentioned that Heat 2's shooting schedule had been delayed, and that he wouldn't start on the production until early December. When asked by Eisen if the delay had been caused by Mann's recent shooting accident at a Los Angeles gun range, Driver insisted that Mann's misfortune hadn't significantly halted production.
"No, [the delay] was already part of the plan," said Driver. "[Mann] is good. I texted him, he immediately responded, [and] he was at work the next day."

articles.title: Pokémon Pokopia Celebrates Fall with Apple-Themed Event
articles.summary: Applin and its Dragon/Grass-type evolutions are coming to Pokémon Pokopia this November thanks to the Apples for Applin event. It's time to start apple-picking so you can trade with Applin and build habitats for all of its friends.
body: Pokémon Pokopia players spent the last couple of weeks playing tricks on Pokémon in exchange for candy. This allowed them to trade with Pumpkaboo and collect Halloween-themed items to decorate their island. That event, Pumpkaboo's Sweet Surprises, is officially over, and gamers only have a few days before the next event.

The Apples for Applin event begins on Nov. 16 at 5 a.m. in-game time. To begin the event, all players need to do is make sure they update their game to version 2.0.1 and log in while connected to the internet. During the event, players will have to look for special apple trees that produce Syrupy Apples. Then, they can hand them to Applin at a Pokémon Center in exchange for event items. The apple-themed items can be placed to create habitats that will attract Applin and its evolutions: Appletun, Flapple, Dipplin, and Hydrapple.

articles.title: Star Wars Actor Officially Confirms the Hunt for Ben Solo Is Dead — and That's a Good Thing.
articles.summary: After months of Star Wars fans campaigning with billboards and banners flown over Disney HQ, Kylo Ren/Ben Solo actor Adam Driver has driven the final nail into the coffin for anyone hoping for a revival of The Hunt for Ben Solo.
body: When Driver revealed that he and director Steven Soderbergh had been working on a secret Lucasfilm project about a redeemed Kylo Ren, the Star Wars fandom erupted. Driver, Soderbergh, and screenwriter Rebecca Blunt believed Kylo Ren still had much more to offer. Although former Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy, vice president Cary Beck, and former chief creative officer — and current Lucasfilm co-president — Dave Filoni were interested, Disney studio executives Bob Iger and Alan Bergman shut the project down.

While it is deeply ironic for Disney’s reason not to continue Kylo Ren’s story due to their inability to see how they could bring Kylo back to life — ignore us pointing to previously dead characters brought back to life, like Darth Maul, Asajj Ventress, and Emperor Palpatine — we can’t say that we’re particularly upset about the loss of The Hunt for Ben Solo. It’s not that Kylo isn’t an intriguing character, far from it. It’s just that, of all the characters the sequel trilogy failed most, Kylo Ren is at the very bottom of the list.

articles.title: How Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Benefits From A Glaringly Obvious Tactic That Few Game Devs Follow
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has been regarded as one of the best games ever made for nearly 30 years, and its new Switch 2 remake is seeing similar levels of acclaim.
body: Speaking to GameSpot, longtime Zelda producer Eiji Aonuma acknowledged the benefits of having developers on the team who have been working at Nintendo for decades.

"I think you see a real benefit to having some very long-term-tenured staff members around who have shared the same experiences over time, because every time you get to the next step, it's easier to discuss how to proceed, or if you're going to do something new," Aonuma said via an interpreter. "When you have new staff coming in, of course you want to make sure that you're bringing everyone up with a lot of discussion, explaining how to do things, why you're doing things certain ways, as well as the language that you're using. But that takes some more time, as well. So you need a bit of a balance."
Despite not having everyone move from one Zelda project to the next, enough developers have remained at Nintendo to provide a consistent throughline.

articles.title: Dragon Ball Composer Is Elected Texas Attorney General
articles.summary: The "blue tsunami" that swept America in the latest midterm elections will be remembered for years to come. Amid all the political turmoil, however, one small detail might go unnoticed: Nathan M. Johnson, who was just elected Attorney General of Texas, used to make music for Dragon Ball.
body: Johnson, who has held the 16th district seat in the Texas Senate since 2018, had a prolific legal and music career before pursuing politics full-time. He owned a music-production company, which produced music for many episodes of the Funimation dub of the Dragon Ball Z anime and five of the franchise's films.

The Funimation dub was the second English dub produced for Dragon Ball Z. The first one, made by Ocean Group, was panned for the excessive cuts and edits to the story imposed by Saban Entertainment. Later, Funimation parted ways with Saban and started producing the dub in-house, creating the version of Dragon Ball Z that most viewers are familiar with. It was a pioneering time for anime in the West, and the popularity of Dragon Ball Z on Cartoon Network's Toonami block contributed to opening the floodgates for what is now one of the most popular forms of entertainment in the world.

articles.title: Nintendo Wanted Ocarina Of Time To Feel Better In The Remake, Not Just Different
articles.summary: Remaking a game like The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time required Nintendo to nail a fine balance between staying faithful to the original and updating it where it mattered.
body: In addition to the changes in the game's controls, Fujibayashi added that the updated graphics also allowed the team to "provide a lot more information" to players, and the sound design also got a big upgrade: 5.1-channel surround sound for the background music.

To reduce friction, the team concluded that a dedicated jump action would give players more agency to explore the world without changing the core experience. "There was a lot of heavy discussion, as you mentioned, about the jump button," Fujibayashi said. "Ultimately, we ended up in the conclusion that being able to allow players to jump anywhere will make the gameplay experience a lot smoother and allow players to be really able to fully enjoy the experience that this game is trying to provide."
The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time launches for Switch 2 on November 5, and it's already one of the year's best-reviewed games.
"The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a reverent remake with stellar presentation, letting the original greatness shine through," Steve Watts wrote in GameSpot's Ocarina of Time remake review.

articles.title: PlayStation sees record high player numbers and increased revenue for Q2 2026, and a lot of that success is down to Marvel's Wolverine
articles.summary: As part of today's (Thursday 5th November, 2026) financial results, Sony has confirmed that monthly active users, referred to as MAU, across both PlayStation 4 and 5, reached 127 million in September. This represents a seven percent growth year-on-year for the company, and sets a new record high.
body: In Layman's terms, this simply means that more people are engaged with the PlayStation ecosystem now than ever before. And it's not just that there are more people using machines and occasionally booting up their consoles; active play time also increased over the past quarter, too, with total logged play time increasing by four percent, year-on-year. As a result, Sony and PlayStation noted that its Game & Network Services division saw revenue grow by nine percent year-on-year, resulting in operating profit rising by 83 percent year-on-year.

Notably, despite its mixed reception, Marvel's Wolverine was name-checked as a driving force for the decent performance over the past quarter - but that shouldn't be a surprise for anyone that's actually been paying attention to how the game performed. The game sold through 2.4 million copies as of 4th November (so, in roughly 50 days). Ghost of Yotei, meanwhile, has sold through 3.3 million since its launch in October 2025.

articles.title: Our Big Interview With Ocarina of Time Producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi
articles.summary: The leaders of Zelda reflect on the series as they guide a new generation of developers.
body: “There are much younger developers who are working on this game, and I do think this is a really valuable experience for them to familiarize themselves first with the original Ocarina of Time and then have their own reinterpretation of it,” Aonuma said. “And to have those conversations throughout the course of development that may aid them in future projects as well.”

This is just one way the pair is reflecting on this franchise they’ve spent decades working on. I spoke to Aonuma and Fujibayashi for nearly an hour ahead of the release of Ocarina of Time, and we discussed the elements that make a Zelda game, how real-world inspirations and expertise play into game development at Nintendo, and their strongest memories and reflections as the Zelda franchise celebrates its 40th anniversary. Read on for my full conversation, including one of Aonuma’s key memories with Zelda creator Shigeru Miyamoto: "Hey, Mr. Aonuma, you know you can't really cut a wooden crate with a sword, right?"
IGN: It is great to meet you both. I'd like to start by congratulating you on tonight's launch of the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, as well as the 40th anniversary of The Legend of Zelda.

articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever is off to a great start with Blizzard's smoothest launch in memory
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever came out last night. Those who stayed up were prepared for the usual from major WoW releases: long queues, disconnects, and server lag. However, save for a few minor hiccups here and there, things went off without a hitch.
body: Eurogamer can report first-hand that for European players who stayed up from, let's say 11pm - 3:50am last night, the login queues were short and constantly moving. Those who were very keen to get in the moment servers went live ran into unclickable server selection boxes, but backing out and re-joining the short queue fixed this problem swiftly.

Once you got in, there was very little server lag save for a lost spell cast or two, nor were constant random disconnects that would boot you out into the cold (I didn't get disconnected once - a record). As far as WoW launches go, an incredibly smooth first day.

This was acknowledged by World of Warcraft developers, such as executive producer Holly Longdale who wrote on X: "At the risk of jinxing things, so far so goodish which is crazy by itself. The team prepared a lot since the wildness of Beta. And this launch was crazier than the insanity we imagined but thankfully the team built plans and contingencies. They are incredible in my opinion.".

articles.summary: Today, Thursday 5th November, 2026, Sony shared its latest financial results, reporting on the second quarter of financial year 2026 for the company. In a wide-ranging set of statements, we learned that the company's overall profits have been charged by the box office success of Spider-Man: Brand…
body: As for PlayStation, Sony CFO Lin Tao hinted at the status of the PlayStation 6 - not yet named as such - which is currently being worked on in the company's gaming division. She noted that the console is "progressing as scheduled" and that staff are making "solid progress" on the machine (thanks, VGC ). Tao also revealed that it's been a strong year for the PS5; total sales for the console have reached 97.9 million, thanks to a further 2.6 million sales throughout July, August and September 2026.

The most interesting bytes of information teased out of this call relate to Tao's claim that Sony has been able to offset the rise in memory costs via cost reductions and price increases, all helped by a yearly operating income boost of 89 percent. Sony notes that it has secured enough memory hardware for its next business year, which helps prepare the ground for PlayStation 6 production which should kick off in earnest next year.

articles.title: Oh hell yes: Pillars of Eternity 1 and 2 are getting full-fat gamepad support and you can try it right now
articles.summary: Reader, a confession: each night, before I retire to my chambers, I light a small votive candle. Bowing over it, I clasp my hands and beseech the ghost of Josh Sawyer (who is not dead) to return to the Pillars of Eternity games and add the weirdly-decent gamepad support they got on console to their…
body: My prayers are answered. In an announcement yesterday, Obsidian declared that now is the time of the Pillars of Eternity and Deadfire: Controller Support Public Test. Both PoE 1 and 2 have ongoing Steam betas that will allow you to play with full, start-to-finish controller support. You can opt into them and try the new feature for yourself by visiting each game's properties and opting into their respective November 4 beta versions.

Being betas, they're a touch buggy right now. Indeed, one of Obsidian's very first notices to players in the public test's announcement is "This is a public test, so please expect bugs", but I'm nevertheless impressed by the limited time I've spent mucking around with the games on Steam Deck.

There are a couple of misaligned gamepad prompts here, a very slight amount of awkwardness with the analogue movement there, but frankly my main takeaway is 'Dang, it's kind of wild how well these isometric CRPGs adjust to non-keyboard-and-mouse support'. Which, yeah, is how I felt about the console versions too.
The public test runs until November 25, and the devs will use the data gathered to iron out wrinkles like those I just listed for a full release.

articles.title: Valve explains why it's running behind on Steam game approvals, asks developers to perform basic release checks to prevent re-reviews
articles.summary: In the wake of witnessing an unprecedented number of game submissions to Steam over the last few months, Valve has been forced to delay approvals in order to deal with the existing backlog.
body: Following complaints by game developers on social media and elsewhere, Valve has now responded to explain why it's taking longer to get games approved. The short version: re-reviews are clogging up the system.

"We aim to test every game build in a timely manner, typically within three-five business days," Valve wrote in a Steam post. "However, we're running a little behind right now and taking up to 12 business days. Much of that delay is due to having to re-review games, which isn't great for you or for us."

As Valve explained in the post, games need to be re-reviewed when they're rejected for missing key quality assurance checks. In an effort to make it easier for developers to get it right the first time, Valve updated the Steam release checklist to include new, tighter requirements.
These include a requirement to run the game through Steam for at least five minutes. According to Valve, some of the games submitted have not been played through Steam.

Here are the biggest changes we found to The Ocarina of Time Remake on Switch 2 – spoilers ahead!

videos.title: Ocarina of Time - Original vs Remake Comparison
videos.summary: Enjoy this graphics comparison of the original N64 version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and the brand new Switch 2 remake.
body: This video will cover from the beginning of the game up to getting the Master Sword.
Footage of the N64 version is captured from an original NTSC 1.0 cartridge running on an Analogue 3D with de-blur enabled.
